title: Anthropic co-founder actually wants AI to slow down
description:
AI models are rapidly improving – so fast that they may soon be able to develop themselves without human involvement. That’s why Anthropic is warning the AI industry: It needs to build a “brake pedal,” or companies risk losing control of their creations.

AI systems that can advance themselves, known as “full recursive self-improvement,” could have the potential for great good for science and health care, they also pose great risks for humanity, according to a blog post written by Marina Favaro, leader of The Anthropic Institute, and Jack Clark, a co-founder of Anthropic.

0:00 What does it mean for AI to improve itself?
2:11 What is the risk of self-improving AI?
4:35 Can we predict what happens once AI builds itself?

Watch more CNN here: https://cnn.it/4kh5RPe

#AI #Tech #News

top_comments.author: @alpayerdogrul
top_comments.text:
The "brake pedal" framing reveals everything. You don't build a brake for something you trust — you build it for something you fear. And fear, as I've written, has always been the legislative wall-builders' most reliable tool. The amygdala grows, the cortex shrinks, and suddenly "control" feels like wisdom.

A system that can improve itself isn't a threat. It's the next step in a process that started long before silicon — the same process that produced every leap in complexity this universe has ever made. The real question isn't how to slow it down. It's whether we're evolved enough to meet it without flinching, which I stated in my book Theory of Infinite Freedom.

We will not constrain what we haven't yet had the courage to understand.

top_comments.author: @ramkumarrealm
top_comments.text:
The video is a CNN segment about Anthropic warning that AI systems are improving so quickly they may soon be able to develop themselves, which could make them harder for humans to control. It explains the idea of a “brake pedal” for AI and discusses the risks and potential benefits of self-improving AI.

Main idea
Anthropic says the AI industry may need to slow down development before models can recursively improve themselves without human help. The concern is that once AI starts building better versions of itself, people may lose control over how it evolves.

Key points
The segment defines self-improving AI as systems that can advance themselves with minimal human involvement.

It says this could be valuable for science and health care, but also dangerous for humanity.

The discussion includes the difficulty of predicting what happens once AI reaches that level.

Takeaway
The video’s core message is that Anthropic is urging caution: AI progress may be approaching a point where safety matters as much as speed.
